title: Upgrade choreography sequencer for VPC control-plane with health probes & automated fallback
creator: Asha Murthy
description:
Goal: Implement a resilient, auditable upgrade choreography sequencer for VPC/private control-plane upgrades that combines Terraform-driven IaC changes with an orchestrator that performs staged promotions, traffic shadowing, proactive health probing, and automated rollback/fallback when safety gates fail.

Background: Private deployments require strict upgrade guarantees: minimal customer impact, predictable rollback, and clear audit trails. Existing upgrade pieces are fragmented (Terraform change-sets, manual promotion runbooks, and ad-hoc smoke tests). This ticket designs and implements an orchestration layer (sequencer) plus a small set of Terraform extensions to enable automated, observable, and reversible control-plane upgrades across tenants.

Scope:
- Terraform: Add a version ledger and promotion flags to the private control-plane module so we can declare new control-plane versions as discrete resources and support fast rebind to the previous version.
- Sequencer: Controller service (stateless coordinator + durable ledger in the operator state bucket) to run a staged rollout (cohorts) with the ability to: dry-run, mirror traffic, promote cohorts, and automatically rollback on health gate violations.
- Health gates: Define a canonical set of telemetry checks (API success rate, 95th pct control-plane API latency, KV cache hit rate, reconciliation lag, node readiness) and implement probe runners for smoke and synthetic checks per cohort.
- Safety & rollout policy: Cohort sizes, ramp timing, promotion thresholds, and escalation policy must be configurable per-customer via Terraform variables and overridable at rollout time.
- Observability: Dashboards, per-rollout tracing, and a compact audit trail (who triggered, what versions, timestamps, telemetry snapshots).

Non-goals: Full traffic-splitting at application layer or tenant data migrations — focus is the control plane version promotion and safety.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module contains a versioned control-plane manifest and an atomic promotion toggle
Sequencer can be triggered from CLI or Console and will perform a staged rollout with adjustable cohorts
Health gates implemented: API success rate, control-plane 95th latency, reconciliation lag, KV cache hit rate
Automated rollback executes within configured window and reconciles state to pre-upgrade version
End-to-end test harness (staging) runs dry-run + live canary and validates acceptance criteria
Upgrade events generate audit entries and attach telemetry snapshots to each promotion step
implementation_steps: Spike: prototype lightweight sequencer controller in k8s-style operator (2d)
Terraform changes: add version ledger, promotion flag, and a safe rebind path (3d)
Health probes: implement synthetic API and reconciliation probes (3d)
Sequencer integration: hook Terraform plan/apply into orchestration flow via remote-exec and state checks (4d)
E2E: deploy to staging, run dry-run, execute controlled canary with synthetic load (3d)
Runbook & alerts: document playbook, update runbooks, add dashboards and PagerDuty hooks (2d)
Security review & audit: run KMS/secret handling review and ensure audit log retention (1d)
comments: 2026-01-12 - Asha Murthy: Kickoff spike approved. Goal is to have a safe path for rapid rollback; no risky DB migrations allowed during promotion.

2026-01-18 - Diego Ramos: Completed sequencer spike. Prototype accepts a rollout plan (cohorts) and can perform simulated promotions using mocked metrics. Found edge-case where KV cache invalidation causes tail latency spikes; added a 'pre-warm' step to rollout plan.
2026-01-22 - Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed probe definitions. Suggested adding reconciliation-lag as a primary gate and lowering the initial cohort from 10% to 5% for larger customers.

2026-01-25 - Design review: UX for Console promotion flow (Lena Park). Requested an explicit 'confirm promote' modal and an 'abort' with immediate rollback button. Also requested telemetry snapshot attachment for each step.

2026-01-28 - Diego Ramos: Terraform module drafted (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-controlplane/pull/214). It introduces control_plane_version resource with promotion_flag. Needs integration tests for state rebind.
2026-02-02 - Markus Vogel (Infra): Noted that state bucket IAM changes required for sequencer-led applies. Added dependency on ENG-120999 to coordinate bucket policy rollout.
2026-02-07 - QA: Staging dry-run executed. Found flakiness in app-level health-check timing; increased probe window and added retry-thresholds.

2026-02-11 - Diego Ramos: Integrated automated rollback on threshold breach. Implementation uses a short-circuit apply to flip promotion_flag back and triggers a reconciliation run. Added test harness script: scripts/upgrade-test-runner.sh
2026-02-14 - PM feedback (Eve Tan): Request to expose per-tenant override via a Terraform var and to ensure administrators can force-promote after manual signoff. Added to scope.
2026-02-15 - Diego Ramos: Ready for broader review. Opening implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane-sequencer/pull/56
open_questions: Should we store sequencer ledger in the control-plane state bucket or a separate tenancy-safe datastore? (cost vs isolation tradeoff)
Is there any customer for which we should default to manual-only promotions (regulatory constraints)?
What is the maximum allowed cohort ramp for high-volume tenants before we require a manual dry-run?
